items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 1 ounce of useable cannabis bought from a licensed retailer. Opening or using cannabis in public or in view of the public (parks, sidewalks, restaurants, federal land) is illegal; private use where the owner allows.

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over (residents or not, with government ID) may buy and possess 1 ounce of usable cannabis, 16 oz of solid edibles, 72 oz of drinks and 7 g of concentrate. Public use is not allowed. It is illegal to take cannabis out of Washington, including on a plane; in a car it must stay sealed and in the boot. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.

Seattle's Parks Code bans drinking alcohol or holding an open container of it in a city park unless Seattle Parks and the state Liquor and Cannabis Board have given a permit; carrying an unopened container is also barred with narrow exceptions (Seattle Municipal Code 18.12.255 and 18.12.257). Alcohol is also listed as prohibited at the beach fire rings at Alki Beach and Golden Gardens.

Seattle's parks are smoke-free: Parks Code of Conduct rule 3.2.10 bans smoking cigars, cigarettes, hookahs, tobacco or other smoking material in the publicly accessible parts of Parks property. The 2017 notice excludes electronic vaping devices from the rule and says smoking on sidewalks and public rights-of-way is not covered. Enforcement is by reminders, rangers, police and written trespass warnings. The notice is from 2017, so recheck the current wording.

Beach fires in Seattle are allowed only at Alki Beach and Golden Gardens Park, only in the installed fire rings (first come, first served), with clean dry firewood, no amplified music, and the fire out by 9:30 p.m. Rings unlock at 4 p.m. and the 2021 season ran 29 May to 12 September; the rules sit in Seattle Municipal Code 18.12.270. Recheck current dates.

In Washington state parks, possessing or drinking alcohol is allowed only in designated campsites and overnight accommodation (by registered occupants and guests), designated picnic areas (any area with tables, benches or fireplaces), permitted reservable group day-use facilities and licensed concession areas, and not in parks posted closed to alcohol. The parks agency lists Dash Point, Flaming Geyser, Saltwater and Sacajawea parks and the Little Spokane River Natural Area as closed to alcohol. Glass bottles and metal cans are not allowed on swim beaches. (WAC 352-32-210)

In Washington state parks only campfires, and fires for stoves, candles, torches, barbecues and charcoal, are allowed. Campfires must stay in the campfire pit, ring or enclosure provided, with flames no higher than two feet. On ocean beaches a recreational fire must be at least 100 feet from the dunes and no more than four feet across and four feet high, and none are allowed on shellfish beds. Rangers can add limits. Fireworks, firecrackers and explosives are prohibited in any state park area, except display permits issued by the director. (WAC 352-32-125 and 352-32-140)

Consumer fireworks in Washington: sale and discharge are restricted to certain times around the July 4 holiday and New Year's Eve, set by state law (RCW 70.77), and local governments can restrict them further, so many cities and counties ban them. The State Patrol's State Fire Marshal page publishes the dates as a chart; ask the local fire department before buying or using any.

layers.authority: USDA Forest Service, Alpine Lakes Wilderness (via recreation.gov)
layers.process: Overnight use in the Enchantments needs a permit from 15 May to 31 October (self-register at the trailhead outside those dates). Advance lottery runs each February (exact 2026 dates not on the page). Fees: US$6 (about A$8.50) lottery application, non-refundable; US$5 (about A$7) per person per day. Zones: Core Enchantment, Snow Lake, Colchuck Lake, Stuart Lake, Eightmile/Caroline. Groups up to eight including stock; one permit per person per season; no dogs. Leavenworth Ranger District 509-548-2550. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Mount Rainier National Park
layers.process: A wilderness permit is required year-round for all overnight stays in the backcountry; none for day hiking. Climbing above 10,000 feet or on glaciers needs a climbing permit. For June to October, about two thirds of permits can be reserved on Recreation.gov (at least 2 days ahead); the rest are walk-up at Wilderness Information Centers, up to a day before. An optional early-access lottery for Wonderland Trail and popular climbing routes opens each February; general on-sale starts 25 April. Fee: US$6 booking fee (about A$8.50) plus US$12 per person per night (about A$17). You must collect the printed permit in person from a ranger; a reservation is cancelled if you do not arrive by 12 noon on the start day. The park entrance fee is extra. The Carbon River and Mowich Lake area was inaccessible on the page's date (bridge closure). Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
